q-341226.name: Question 1
q-341226.worked_solution:
If $F(x)$ is defined on $x\in [0,5),$ the odd extension of $F$ is the function $f$ such that

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}F(x), & x\in [0,5), \\ -F(-x), & x\in (-5,0).\end{aligned}
$$

In our cases, for $x\in (-5,0),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =-F(-x) \\  & =-(-x){e}^{3(-x-1)} \\  & =x{e}^{3(-x-1)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-1) & =(-1){e}^{3(-(-1)-1)}=-{e}^{3(0)}=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

q-338784.name: Question 2
q-338784.problem: Let $F(x)={x}^{2}-2x$ for $x\in [0,\pi ),$ and let $f(x)$ be the **odd** extension of $F(x)$ to $x\in (-\pi ,\pi ).$ What is $f(x)$ for $x\in (-\pi ,0)?$
q-338784.worked_solution:
If $F(x)$ is defined on $x\in [0,\pi ),$ the odd extension of $F$ is the function $f$ such that

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}F(x), & x\in [0,\pi ), \\ -F(-x), & x\in (-\pi ,0).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, for $x\in (-\pi ,0),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =-F(-x) \\  & =-((-x)^{2}-2(-x)) \\  & =-({x}^{2}+2x) \\  & =-{x}^{2}-2x.\end{aligned}
$$

q-340708.name: Question 6
q-340708.problem:
$$
f(x)∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)
$$

Let $F(x)=2$ for $x\in [0,\pi ).$ The Fourier sine series of the **odd** $2\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the expression for ${b}_{n}.$
$\,{b}_{n}=$ {{field-1}}
q-340708.worked_solution:
For our Fourier sine series, the coefficients are given by

$$
{b}_{n}=\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }f(x)\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $f(x)=2$ for $x\in (0,\pi ).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{n} & =\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }2\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{4}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{4}{n\pi }[\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)]_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =-\frac{4}{n\pi }(\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)) \\  & =\frac{4(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi ))}{n\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since $\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )=(-1)^{n},$ we have

$$

q-340906.problem:
$$
f(x)∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)
$$

Let $F(x)=-4$ for $x\in [0,\pi ).$ The Fourier sine series of the **odd** $2\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the expression for ${b}_{n}.$$\,{b}_{n}=$ {{field-1}}
q-340906.worked_solution:
For our Fourier sine series, the coefficients are given by

$$
{b}_{n}=\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }f(x)\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $f(x)=-4$ for $x\in (0,\pi ).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{n} & =\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }(-4)\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{8}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{8}{n\pi }[\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)]_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =\frac{8}{n\pi }(\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)) \\  & =\frac{8(\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )-1)}{n\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since $\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )=(-1)^{n},$ we have

$$
{b}_{n}=\frac{8((-1)^{n}-1)}{\pi n}.
$$

Question 7

f(x)∼∑n=1∞bnsin⁡(nx) Let F(x)=−4 for x∈[0,π). The Fourier sine series of the odd 2π-periodic extension f(x) of F(x) is shown above. Find the expression for bn.bn=
8((−1)n−1)πn
8(1−(−1)n)πn
4((−1)n−1)πn
4(1−(−1)n)πn
((−1)n−1)8πn
8((−1)n−1)πn
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For our Fourier sine series, the coefficients are given by bn=2π∫0πf(x)sin⁡(nx)dx.

In our case, f(x)=−4 for x∈(0,π). So, substituting into the formula, we get

bn=2π∫0π(−4)sin⁡(nx)dx=−8π∫0πsin⁡(nx)dx=8nπ[cos⁡(nx)]0π=8nπ(cos⁡(nπ)−cos⁡(0))=8(cos⁡(nπ)−1)nπ.

Finally, since cos⁡(nπ)=(−1)n, we have bn=8((−1)n−1)πn.

q-340927.name: Question 8
q-340927.problem:
$$
f(x)∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)
$$

Let $F(x)=6x$ for $x\in [0,\pi ).$ The Fourier sine series of the **odd** $2\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the expression for ${b}_{n}.$$\,{b}_{n}=$ {{field-1}}
q-340927.worked_solution:
For our Fourier sine series, the coefficients are given by

$$
{b}_{n}=\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }f(x)\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $f(x)=6x$ for $x\in (0,\pi ).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
{b}_{n}=\frac{12}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }x\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x.
$$

We use the integration by parts: 

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⇒\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\, & ⇒\,v=-\frac{1}{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{n} & =\frac{12}{\pi }(uv\,{|}_{0}^{\pi }-{\int }_{0}^{\pi }v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{12}{\pi }(-\frac{1}{n}[x\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)]_{0}^{\pi }+\frac{1}{n}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{12}{\pi }(-\frac{1}{n}(\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )-0\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(0))+\frac{1}{n}{[\frac{1}{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)]}_{0}^{\pi }) \\  & =\frac{12}{\pi }(-\frac{\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )}{n}+\frac{1}{{n}^{2}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0))) \\  & =-\frac{12\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )}{n}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since $\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )=(-1)^{n},$ we have

$$
{b}_{n}=-\frac{12(-1)^{n}}{n}=\frac{12(-1)^{n+1}}{n}.
$$

q-340922.name: Question 9
q-340922.problem:
Let $F(x)=-3x$ for $x\in [0,\pi ).$ Select the correct missing parts in the Fourier sine series of the **odd** $2\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of the function $F(x)$ below.

$$
f(x)∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,{{field-1}}\cdot {{field-2}}
$$
q-340922.worked_solution:
For our Fourier sine series, the coefficients are given by

$$
{b}_{n}=\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }f(x)\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $f(x)=-3x$ for $x\in (0,\pi ).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
{b}_{n}=-\frac{6}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }x\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x.
$$

We use the integration by parts: 

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⇒\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\, & ⇒\,v=-\frac{1}{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{n} & =-\frac{6}{\pi }(uv\,{|}_{0}^{\pi }-{\int }_{0}^{\pi }v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x) \\  & =-\frac{6}{\pi }(-\frac{1}{n}[x\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)]_{0}^{\pi }+\frac{1}{n}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{6}{n\pi }((\pi \cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )-0\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(0))-\frac{1}{n}[\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)]_{0}^{\pi }) \\  & =\frac{6}{n\pi }(\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )-\frac{1}{n}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0))) \\  & =\frac{6\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )}{n}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, since $\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )=(-1)^{n},$ we have

$$
{b}_{n}=\frac{6(-1)^{n}}{n}.
$$

Finally, the Fourier sine series is

$$
f(x)∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{6(-1)^{n}}{n}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(nx).
$$

Let $F(x)=3$ for $x\in [0,\pi ).$ The Fourier sine series of the **odd** $2\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the expression for ${b}_{n}.$$\,{b}_{n}=$ {{field-1}}

For our Fourier sine series, the coefficients are given by

$$
{b}_{n}=\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }f(x)\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $f(x)=3$ for $x\in (0,\pi ).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{n} & =\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }3\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{6}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{6}{n\pi }[\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)]_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =-\frac{6}{n\pi }(\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)) \\  & =\frac{6(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi ))}{n\pi }.\end{aligned}

$$

$$

Question 10
?
f(x)∼∑n=1∞bnsin⁡(nx) Let F(x)=3 for x∈[0,π). The Fourier sine series of the odd 2π-periodic extension f(x) of F(x) is shown above. Find the expression for bn.bn=
6(1−(−1)n)πn
6(1−(−1)n)πn
3(1+(−1)n)πn
(1−(−1)n)6πn
6(1+(−1)n)πn
3(1−(−1)n)πn
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For our Fourier sine series, the coefficients are given by bn=2π∫0πf(x)sin⁡(nx)dx.

In our case, f(x)=3 for x∈(0,π). So, substituting into the formula, we get

bn=2π∫0π3sin⁡(nx)dx=6π∫0πsin⁡(nx)dx=−6nπ[cos⁡(nx)]0π=−6nπ(cos⁡(nπ)−cos⁡(0))=6(1−cos⁡(nπ))nπ.

Finally, since cos⁡(nπ)=(−1)n, we have bn=6(1−(−1)n)πn.
